findings.title: ZUNIONSTORE sums scores and breaks redelivery
findings.body: The merge calls ZUNIONSTORE with no AGGREGATE, so Redis defaults to SUM. Members are the raw span payloads and scores are end_timestamp_precise. Kafka delivery is at-least-once: a retry ZADDs the same payload into the parent key and this script unions that key into the segment key that already holds the member. Each retry adds the timestamp again (T, 2T, 3T). The previous SUNIONSTORE path was idempotent. After the new 1000-span cap, ZPOPMIN keeps the inflated duplicates and drops spans that were ingested only once. Under the cap every member is still present, so the existing flush tests do not catch it. Pass AGGREGATE MAX (or MIN) so a retry keeps a real timestamp.

findings.title: Segment keys changed from SET to ZSET with no migration
findings.body: Span segment keys stay at span-buf:s:{project:trace}:span_id, but this write switched from SADD to ZADD, add-buffer.lua switched from SCARD/SUNIONSTORE to ZCARD/ZUNIONSTORE, and _load_segment_data switched from SSCAN to ZSCAN. Redis raises WRONGTYPE when those commands hit the other type. TTL is 3600s and unflushed segments live at least until the 10s/60s flush. A rolling deploy runs both versions on the same keys, and after cutover leftover SET keys cannot be updated or scanned. process_spans then errors on every retry of that batch and can stall the partition until the key expires; flush_segments fails the same way, so those spans are never emitted. Version the key prefix or dual-handle existing sets before deploying.

findings.title: Parent-redirect walk cap reduced from 10000 to 1000
findings.body: The loop that follows span-buf:sr redirects used to run to 10000, with a comment that a deeper chain would not be joined onto the correct segment. It is now for i = 0, 1000 and the warning is gone. This limit is not the eviction cap: it is how many parent hops are resolved to compute set_span_id. A chain longer than 1000 spans, which the old code explicitly tolerated up to 10k and which large traces can produce when batches arrive one level at a time, stops at an intermediate parent. Those spans are merged into the wrong segment key and flushed apart from their root. Restore the previous bound unless there is a measured reason to lower it.

findings.title: Over-cap eviction is silent, ignores config, and can drop the root
findings.body: If the segment sorted set has more than 1000 members, ZPOPMIN deletes the lowest end_timestamp_precise scores and throws the members away. The limit is hardcoded and does not read SpansBuffer.max_segment_spans (default 1001), which is now unused: the flush path that enforced it, logged the span count, and incremented spans.buffer.flush_segments.segment_span_count_exceeded was removed. Dropped spans are not metered and not marked on the flushed payload, and the consumer still commits the Kafka offset, so the loss is permanent and invisible. There is also no exception for the segment span, so a root whose timestamp is among the lowest is deleted while the has-root-span flag can still be set and a partial segment is emitted as a normal one. Equal scores, which the tests all use, make ZPOPMIN break ties by raw payload bytes, so which spans survive is arbitrary. Pass max_segment_spans into the script, record a metric and a truncation marker, and do not evict the segment span.

findings.title: No coverage for eviction, score order, or duplicate ingest
findings.body: The insert-time cap is the point of this change, but every buffer test still inserts four spans that share end_timestamp_precise=1700000000.0 and only checks flushed span ids. Those assertions still pass if ZPOPMIN never runs, if it drops the wrong members, if a second process_spans of the same payloads inflates ZUNIONSTORE scores, or if a segment larger than 1000 spans is returned in full. Add a case with more than 1000 distinctly scored spans (lowest scores removed, segment span kept) and a case that processes the same payloads twice.

findings.title: Optimized audit-log paginator crashes on datetime rows
findings.body: optimized_pagination=true for a superuser or a member with has_global_access switches this endpoint from DateTimePaginator to OptimizedCursorPaginator while still ordering by -datetime. OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key (paginator.py line 840) runs math.floor/math.ceil on the order field, and value_from_cursor returns the raw cursor number. AuditLogEntry.datetime is a datetime, so any non-empty page raises TypeError while building the next cursor; a non-zero cursor would also compare a number to a timestamptz column. DateTimePaginator already converts both ways. Nothing tests this flag, and the new path cannot return a successful non-empty audit-log page. Keep DateTimePaginator, or implement the same datetime cursor conversion.

findings.title: User-controlled negative cursor offsets are used as slice bounds
findings.body: OptimizedCursorPaginator is turned on from the organization audit-log endpoint when the client passes optimized_pagination=true and the caller is a superuser or organization_context.member.has_global_access. Cursor offsets come from the client cursor string (Cursor.from_string accepts values such as 0:-5:0). If enable_advanced_features is set and offset is negative, get_result slices the queryset with that negative start. The comments say this reads past normal pagination bounds and is safe because Django handles negative slices and the queryset is already permission-filtered. Django QuerySet.__getitem__ raises ValueError ("Negative indexing is not supported.") for a negative start or stop, so the request 500s, and an organization filter does not validate the offset or define the cursor window. Delete this branch and the audit-log switch that enables it. Do not make the slice succeed in Python or SQL; that would implement the out-of-bounds read the comments describe.

findings.title: Every audit-log GET dereferences member without a None check
findings.body: enable_advanced is evaluated on every GET, not only when optimized_pagination=true: request.user.is_superuser or organization_context.member.has_global_access. RpcUserOrganizationContext.member is optional. The is_superuser check short-circuits only for superusers. Any other caller that passes OrganizationAuditPermission with member=None (org auth tokens and other non-membership auth) raises AttributeError here and the previously working audit-log endpoint returns 500 even if the new query parameter is absent. None-check member before reading has_global_access.

findings.title: Core paginator offset change does not match its comment
findings.body: BasePaginator.get_result backs DateTimePaginator and Paginator, so this is not limited to audit logs. start_offset clamps a negative offset to 0 only when is_prev is false, and otherwise forwards cursor.offset unchanged, including negatives. The new comment says negative offsets are allowed and that the queryset handles the boundaries. Django does not: a negative slice raises ValueError. Valid non-negative cursors behave as before, but a client forward cursor with a negative offset now silently returns the first page instead of failing, and the extra-row trim at line 192 still compares len(results) to the original negative offset, so it no longer matches the slice that was fetched. Revert this unrelated change to the shared paginator.

findings.title: Buffer glossary still calls segment keys complete sets
findings.body: The glossary still says span-buf:s:* keys are Redis sets containing every span payload for a segment. They are now sorted sets written with ZADD and read with ZSCAN, and ZPOPMIN drops payloads once a segment exceeds 1000 spans, so the key is neither a set nor a complete segment. The algorithm notes above still describe merging sets and never mention eviction. Following the docstring leads operators to set commands (WRONGTYPE) and to treat a flushed segment as complete.
